newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian commodity prices rise in February.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian commodity prices rise in February.

text.p: Commodity prices in Australian dollar terms rose marginally in February, according to an international commodity price review released on Monday by the National Farmers' Federation (NFF) and Dresdner Australia Ltd.
NFF's Economic Policy Director Todd Ritchie said the improvement was led by price rises in rural commodities, such as sorghum, barley and beef, partially offset by weaker energy prices.
Live cattle prices continued to strengthen and wool prices remained steady, Ritchie said.
The upward movement in commodity prices and the diminishing chance of another interest rate cut suggested the Australian dollar could start to strengthen in the coming months, he said.
Rural prices in special drawing rights (SDR) terms increased by 2.6 percent in February, and were 3.9 percent higher than a year before, he said.
The Dresdner commodity price index, measured in SDR terms increased by 0.5 percent in February, and was 4.1 percent higher than a year before.

"The Eastern Market Indicator for wool averaged around 600 cents/kg, while the improvement in beef prices has been due to a steady firming of the US manufactured beef market, as a result of a slow down in the US cow kill," he said.
Dresdner chief economist Rob Henderson said the non-rural SDR prices had fallen by 0.6 percent in February, and were 3.9 percent higher than a year before.
"Energy prices were 1.4 percent weaker during the month, as a result of weaker prices for petroleum products, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and crude oil," Henderson said.

"Expectation of a continuation of the G-7 economic recovery is likely to support commodity prices in 1997, and there would be little standing in the way of a stronger A$, especially if the possibility of a Reserve Bank of Australia cut diminishes further," he said.
